Maintainer risk: LOW — diff is mostly mechanical (extras-preservation policy adoption per workspace AGENTS.md, jscontact-types consumption, UTCDate type migration). No new public-API surface that locks in a wrong shape. The localizations type change is breaking at the Rust level but byte-identical on the wire, and no external workspace caller existed. Findings filed are documentation drift and canonical-template divergence — both fixable without breaking changes.
Confidence: ~5% chance of missed bug. Least confident flags: none — the only place a serde-flatten-extras shape can silently misbehave is when a renamed field collides with an unknown wire field, and ContactCard / AddressBook / AddressBookRights have no slash-keyed or otherwise-renamed fields that could collide. ContactCardFilterCondition has slash-keyed fields but no flatten-extras, so no collision possible there. Uncertainty driven by: (1) not exercising the type from a downstream server crate in this review (jmap-contacts-server doesn't exist yet, so there's no real-world consumer pressure on the API shape); (2) UTCDate is a transparent String newtype with no validation, so created/updated/created_before/etc. accept any string — but that's a jmap-types property, not introduced by this diff. Would raise confidence if: a jmap-contacts-server stub existed exercising at least Mailbox/get, ContactCard/get, ContactCard/query, and ContactCard/set; or if cargo-public-api was run against the prior tag to surface every API change from the localizations / UTCDate migration.
API contract risk: MEDIUM — the contract is workable but has one silent-wire-corruption hazard (addressBookIds/members MUST be true is not enforced) and four real downstream-burden gaps (22 sloppy fields with no typed accessor, comparator.property has no const pool, 30+ jscontact re-exports with no stability contract, ContactCard::default() emits wire-invalid {}). Filed nine findings (JMAP-glx8.11-.19) covering five of the six api-contract subsections (no pure-immutability finding warranted; #[non_exhaustive] coverage is solid).
API contract confidence: ~15% chance of a missed issue. Least confident flags: (a) JMAP-glx8.19 extra-Map collision behavior — depends on serde-derive flatten iteration order across serde versions, which I asserted by reading the derive macro mental model but did not actually exercise a compile+round-trip experiment under read-only review constraints; (b) JMAP-glx8.14 const-pool recommendation for comparator.property — I checked workspace AGENTS.md and confirmed the filter-algebra exclusion does NOT forbid const helpers, but did not check sibling crates (jmap-mail-types, jmap-calendars-types) for a workspace stylistic precedent of const pools that would either support or contradict my recommendation. Uncertainty driven by: (1) no downstream consumer crate exists yet for me to grep for the burdens I claim are real (jmap-contacts-server is unwritten — bd JMAP-yfpq territory); (2) I did not compare ContactCard's sloppy-field accessor convention against the existing jmap-calendars-types crate, where the same hybrid pattern is in place and may already document this; (3) I did not run cargo public-api against the prior tag to verify my UTCDate / localizations migration impact analysis was complete.
Idiom rating: ACCEPTABLE — diff is overwhelmingly mechanical (workspace-mandated extras-preservation, doc-comment enum sweeps, String→UTCDate newtype migration improving idiom, hybrid jscontact re-export per workspace policy). Only two genuine Rust-idiom concerns: (1) localizations switched from ordered serde_json::Value to unordered std HashMap, regressing wire-format key-order stability — should be BTreeMap or indexmap::IndexMap (JMAP-glx8.20, P1); (2) the alias type-identity test uses runtime assert_eq! where a compile-time const fn or static_assertions check is the idiomatic Rust form (JMAP-glx8.21, P2, opinion). Everything else either follows workspace policy correctly or is pre-existing and out of this diff's scope. No unsafe in scope, no clippy-grade issues introduced by the diff, no ownership / lifetime smells, no macro misuse.
Rust idiom confidence: ~10% chance of missed issue. Least confident flags: JMAP-glx8.20 — I asserted serde_json::Map defaults to BTreeMap (alphabetical) ordering and that HashMap iteration is non-deterministic, but did not run a multi-key round-trip test to demonstrate the divergence empirically (read-only review). The claim is well-documented in serde_json and std::collections::HashMap docs, but the empirical-confirmation step would raise confidence. Uncertainty driven by: (1) no downstream consumer crate exists yet to expose key-order sensitivity in practice (jmap-contacts-server is unwritten); (2) I did not check whether the workspace might enable serde_json/preserve_order at a parent Cargo.toml level — quick grep showed no such feature flag, but a recursive cargo-tree confirmation would be more thorough; (3) the alias type-identity test (JMAP-glx8.21) is labeled opinion because reasonable test authors disagree on whether runtime serde-roundtrip equality is good-enough proxy for compile-time type identity, and the cost of being wrong is bounded. No unsafe in scope so no soundness uncertainty.
API contract risk (supplement re-run): LOW — 8/9 prior api-contract findings (JMAP-glx8.11-.14, .16-.19) closed via documentation and one typed-shape change (keywords HashMap<String,bool>). The 9th (.15, re-export upstream-coupling) deferred to workspace bead JMAP-84zs as a workspace-policy observation, not a per-crate fix. One new finding filed (JMAP-glx8.22, P3): ContactCardComparator::default() produces is_ascending=false (Rust bool default) but wire-default for absent isAscending is true — a quiet footgun where Default::default() construction yields silent descending sort. Scope is per-crate doc-only; the canonical-template question (drop Default derive on all 4 extension-types comparator siblings to match EmailComparator's ::new(property) pattern) is workspace-API scope and properly belongs on a new sibling-of-JMAP-18qe sweep bead, not this review.

Confidence would rise if a jmap-contacts-server stub existed exercising comparator construction, sort, and capability emission paths.
Idiom supplement re-run (3rd pass): CLEAN — no new findings. Prior idiom-supplement runs already exhausted the diff's Rust-idiom surface: .20 (HashMap key-order regression on localizations) and .21 (runtime assert_eq! vs compile-time type assertion on jscontact alias). Re-reading the diff fresh, every other potential idiom concern is either: (a) workspace policy explicitly endorsed (Sloppy-Value pattern, extras-preservation pattern, filter-algebra const pool vs typed-enum-with-Other(String) — all deliberate), (b) already covered by a non-idiom finding (Default-vs-wire-default at .16/.22, canonical-sibling divergence at .4/.6, .into() friction at const-string call sites tied to .14), or (c) tests using .clone().unwrap() in tests where perf doesn't matter and the alternative is no clearer. No unsafe in scope. No macros in scope. No iterator code in scope. No ownership/lifetime smells. The String → UTCDate newtype migration and Value → HashMap<String, bool> on keywords are both idiom improvements, already documented as GOOD (.7, .8, .9).
Idiom rating: CLEAN — third idiom-supplement pass confirms convergence with no new findings.

## Crypto-security supplement run (Section A-G) — calibration

**Disposition per Section:**

- **Section A (key material lifecycle)**: N/A — no key material types in this crate. The `crypto_keys` field on `ContactCard` is `Option<serde_json::Value>` holding RFC 9553 CryptoKey objects, which themselves hold a URI to a public-key cert (PGP/X.509). This is public reference data, not secret material. No secret-bearing types to audit.
- **Section B (side-channel hygiene)**: N/A — no constant-time-relevant comparisons in this crate. Derived `PartialEq` on data types; no code path branches on a secret value. Type crate has no executable logic that touches secrets.
- **Section C (untrusted input at protocol boundaries)**: 3 findings filed — JMAP-glx8.23 (P2 negative-deserialize test gap), JMAP-glx8.24 (P3 deep-nesting/size-budget docs), JMAP-glx8.25 (P2 extra-field collision runtime detection). This is the live area for a type crate; the deserialize-boundary surface is real.
- **Section D (random source quality)**: N/A — no RNG consumption in this crate. No `OsRng`, no `thread_rng()`, no `Math.random()` analogue.
- **Section E (persistent storage of secrets)**: N/A — no persistence layer. Pure types crate with serde derives only.
- **Section F (logging output safety)**: 1 finding filed — JMAP-glx8.26 (P3 PII-bearing types derive plain Debug). This is the lesser-priority leak. PII vs credential is a meaningful distinction; the workspace has the redaction precedent in `jmap-base-client` for credentials but explicitly not propagated to sibling type crates yet. Filed as crate-scoped docs-only with a workspace decision sub-bead.
- **Section G (algorithm and parameter choice)**: N/A — no cryptographic primitives invoked. The crate ships no `Hash`, no `Sign`, no `Encrypt`. The `cryptoKeys` JSContact field is opaque `serde_json::Value`.

**Sections spent < 10 minutes on:**

- A, B, D, E, G all took <2 minutes each — they are categorically N/A for a pure type crate (no key material, no constant-time comparisons, no RNG, no I/O, no crypto primitives). I read the source to confirm this, not because there might be something to find.
- F took ~5 minutes — checked for Debug-redaction precedent in sibling type crates (none found), confirmed `jmap-base-client` precedent exists, and weighed PII-vs-credential framing before filing as P3.
- C took the majority of the session (~20 minutes) — read all 4 source files in full, reasoned about deserialize boundaries, integer overflow, nested-Value depth, duplicate-key behavior, and Sloppy-Value contract.

**Read all relevant code paths vs only the diff:**

I read **all** of `src/card.rs`, `src/addressbook.rs`, `src/capability.rs`, `src/backend.rs`, and `src/lib.rs` — not just the post-`9c0d34f` diff. Crypto/security defects do not respect diff boundaries; a problem in pre-existing code that the diff exposes is in scope. Confirmed: no `unsafe_code` (forbid set), no `.unwrap()` or `.expect()` in library code (only in `#[cfg(test)]` and rustdoc examples). Cross-checked `jmap-base-client` for the redacting-Debug precedent and `crate-jmap-jscontact-types` for sibling-crate convention.

**Probability of missed P0:**

~3% chance a competent third-party crypto reviewer finds a P0 in this code. A type crate without I/O, without crypto primitives, without persistence, and without RNG consumption has very little P0 surface. The live area is Section C and I worked through it carefully. The sub-1-in-30 chance is for: (a) a serde-derive corner-case in the `#[serde(flatten)]` extras handling that produces parser-divergent JSON in some platform combinations (covered partly by JMAP-glx8.25), (b) a stack-overflow vector through the `Option<serde_json::Value>` sloppy fields that bypasses `serde_json`'s 128-deep recursion limit (very unlikely given serde_json's implementation is mature), (c) a workspace-wide misuse pattern that surfaces specifically through contacts data (e.g., a downstream consumer logs contact PII through `tracing` and a SIEM-shipping integration leaks it — that's the JMAP-glx8.26 territory and is filed P3).

3% < 20% threshold — no separate P1 deep-pass bead needed.

**Findings filed:** 4 (JMAP-glx8.23 P2, .24 P3, .25 P2, .26 P3). All labeled `crypto-security`.

**Convergence signal:** 5/7 sections are N/A by category; 1 section yielded 3 findings; 1 yielded 1 finding. The crate's pure-type-crate posture makes this expected. Re-running this supplement against this same crate at the same commit should produce zero new findings.

**Read-only compliance:** No file edits in tree or /tmp; no `cargo fix`; no formatters; no probes executed. All 4 findings describe their hypothesis + probe for a downstream `/do-beads` session.
Idiom rating: CLEAN — 5th idiom-supplement pass confirms convergence with no new findings.

Walked through every /review-rusty Section 1 subsection systematically against the full diff (1707 lines) and all four source files (card.rs, addressbook.rs, backend.rs, capability.rs, lib.rs):

- Ownership/borrowing: nothing new. Owned types in serde-derived structs are required by the derive macro; test-only .clone().unwrap() is workspace-conventional. The String→UTCDate newtype migration improves on idiom (already noted GOOD at .9).
- Error handling: nothing new. #![forbid(unsafe_code)] set; no .unwrap()/.expect() in library code; rustdoc examples use .unwrap() per workspace doc-test convention.
- Iterators/collections: nothing in scope — pure types crate, no iterator code.
- Type design: considered and rejected one borderline finding (see below). The Default-derive-vs-wire-default mismatch on Comparator is already filed at .22; ContactCard::default() wire-invalid case at .16.
- Trait implementations: nothing new. No types in scope warrant Display/From/AsRef. ContactsAccountCapability legitimately lacks Default (deployment-specific value, not zero-defaultable).
- Lifetime annotations: nothing new. No explicit lifetimes in the diff.
- Unsafe: not in scope (#![forbid(unsafe_code)] at crate root).
- Macros: not in scope (string_enum! moved to jmap-types per JMAP-wk77).
- Clippy/language idioms: cargo clippy -p jmap-contacts-types --all-targets -- -D warnings passes cleanly. Pedantic surfaces only workspace-wide noise (must_use, missing-backticks) not introduced by this diff.

Borderline finding considered and explicitly REJECTED:

ContactCard, ContactCardFilterCondition, and AddressBook lack PartialEq (and AddressBook lacks Eq) where their canonical siblings Email, EmailFilterCondition, and Mailbox in jmap-mail-types derive both. This looks like a canonical-template divergence, but cuts against filing because:

  (a) The canonical crate is itself inconsistent — MailboxFilterCondition in jmap-mail-types/src/mailbox.rs also lacks PartialEq/Eq derives. There is no clean canonical pattern to align to.
  (b) The divergence predates 9c0d34f; the diff did NOT introduce or worsen it. The diff did add PartialEq+Eq+Default to ContactCardComparator (per .4), which is the most that scope warrants.
  (c) /review-rusty Section 1.4 qualifies the missing-derive rule with 'types used in assertions or sets'. Neither holds: tests use field-by-field assertion (because PartialEq isn't derived, but also because the fields-of-interest pattern is the test idiom in use). No downstream caller exists yet (jmap-contacts-server is unwritten, bd:JMAP-yfpq).
  (d) The fix would be additive and non-breaking — a future workspace-API canonical-template sweep can pick it up if real engineering pressure appears.

Filing this would be exactly the speculative finding the workspace anti-bikeshedding policy warns against ('do not manufacture problems to fill space'). The four prior idiom-supplement passes' silence on this was a correct calibration.

Open frontier (.20, .22, .23, .24, .25, .26) contains zero idiom findings — they are correctness (P1, P2, P3), security (P2, P3), and policy items filed by my-oss and crypto-security supplements. Stopping here is correct.
Rust idiom confidence (5th pass): ~3% chance of missed issue.

Least confident flags: the one finding I considered and rejected (PartialEq/Eq missing on ContactCard/ContactCardFilterCondition vs canonical Email/EmailFilterCondition). Reasonable Rust practitioners disagree on whether this is bikeshedding or a real ergonomic regression. The canonical crate's own internal inconsistency (MailboxFilterCondition lacks the same derives) cuts against the 'clean canonical pattern' framing, but doesn't fully neutralise it. If the eventual jmap-contacts-server consumer surfaces a real need to compare ContactCards, this becomes a real finding; until then, it's speculation.

Uncertainty driven by: (1) no downstream consumer crate exists yet (jmap-contacts-server is unwritten — bd:JMAP-yfpq) so a use-site idiom smell would not be visible from this crate alone; (2) workspace does not enable -W clippy::pedantic so I cannot verify that contacts-types-specific pedantic lints would not surface — pedantic is consistently disabled as workspace policy, so this is convergence not gap. The clippy::derive_partial_eq_without_eq lint did NOT fire under pedantic invocation despite AddressBook having PartialEq without Eq when extra: serde_json::Map<String, serde_json::Value> appears compatible with Eq (serde_json::Value derives Eq) — possibly because the macro can't prove Eq for the generic Map at expansion time. Either way the lint is allow-by-default and workspace doesn't enable it.

No unsafe in scope so no soundness uncertainty. Convergence reached. Bikeshedding risk if continued: HIGH. Stopping is correct per AGENTS.md anti-bikeshedding rule.

crate.
